design.title: Design system
design.lead: Every value on this page is read out of the application’s own tokens. Nothing here is a second copy.
design.coloursBody: Each name says what a colour is for, not what it looks like. A theme is one assignment, because every name is a reference into the palette in force.
design.rampBody: Not themeable. These eight are document data, written into every project file, so repainting them would make a saved project disagree with the swatch it was chosen from.
design.liftBody: How much lighter a surface gets when touched. A large surface needs a subtler lift than a small one, so there are two rungs and no more.

home.intro: A channel rack with a step grid, a piano roll, a playlist of clips and a mixer, driven by a three-oscillator synth per channel — or by a recording, or by a song written as text and compiled to notes.
home.tabsBody: The same notes, seen four ways, and a fifth tab that writes them for you.

mcp.title: Control dew from an agent
mcp.lead: dew runs a Model Context Protocol server inside the application, so a coding agent can read and change the project you have open: instruments, effects, the mixer, the notes and the arrangement.
mcp.howBody: Turn it on under Audio → MCP. dew listens on the loopback interface only, so nothing off your machine can reach it. The first time a client connects, dew names it and asks whether to allow it, and whether it may only read or change things too. Every change it makes is one step of your undo history.
mcp.connectBody: The MCP settings panel shows the address and the exact command. The port is not fixed — dew takes the next free one when its own is busy — so copy the command instead of typing it.
mcp.surfaceBody: One address space covers every value in the document. A target, an id, a group and a slot name any parameter of any oscillator, envelope, sample, soundfont, effect, mixer insert or the master. The same four fields say what a curve can be pointed at.
mcp.scoreBody: For anything longer than a few bars, an agent writes dew’s arrangement language and compiles it. The language says what the music is — a key, a progression, rhythms, voicings, a counterpoint — and the compiler works out the notes.

mcpReference.title: MCP reference
mcpReference.lead: Generated from the same table the server dispatches on and the permission check reads. A tool cannot exist without being documented, or be documented differently from how it behaves.
mcpReference.guideLead: dew serves these as MCP resources. A client should read the first before its first call.
mcpReference.undoNote: Every call that changes the project is exactly one undo step, however many entries its batch carried.

score.title: The score language
score.lead: A song written as text and compiled to real patterns, notes and clips. Seven block keywords, and the set is closed.
score.exampleCaption: examples/amber.score — the one CI compiles and renders.
score.noExpressions: There is no expression language: no arithmetic, no variables, no conditionals. That restriction is what makes completion a table lookup, and what lets the grid be computed before anything is generated.

setup.title: Setup
setup.lead: dew builds from source on macOS in three commands. There is no release to download — it is a working prototype, and a download would be a build of this repository.
setup.requirementsBody: macOS, and nothing that is not already on a machine somebody writes software on. brew bundle installs the rest from the Brewfile in the repository root.
setup.buildBody: The first configure fetches JUCE and Catch2 from source — a few seconds, shallow, cached per machine under ~/.cache/CPM. One build is slow and the rest are not.
setup.presetsBody: Presets instead of raw flags, so the flags a build was made with live in the repository and not in somebody’s shell history.
setup.runBody: Then Demos → Getting Started in the menu bar. There are eight, and each one demonstrates a different part of the app.
setup.checkBody: One command, running everything CI runs, in the order that fails cheapest first. The dependency pins and the formatting need no build, so a bad pin or an unformatted file is reported in seconds.
setup.platformNote: macOS only. Nothing here has been built or run on another platform. The parts that could be — the score language compiles under gcc and libstdc++ in CI — are the parts that link nothing.
